If we can get the change in before the end of the week or very early next week (1.0 release), we should do a breaking change on the XPC wire format and encode the absolute path but as the string representation of the path instead of as a URL.

The decoder should preserve compatibility (which it looks like you have with `decodePath`) for a few versions so that persisted config values from older releases continue to work.

We could in a separate PR add a persistent config migration at containers service startup in the API server.

This is... crummy (and fragile) that we need to do this. There has to be a better way we can just include at least the volume name in what we send over. The `.block` Filesystem type has everything we need except the volume name which we need to dec the refcount right? I honestly wouldn't be opposed to (I know, we were the ones who told you to use .block) a new FS type that is literally just .block, but with a volume name included. OR just extend .block to include an optional volumeName parameter potentially
Agree - lets avoid checking the path and making a guess based off of that

It might be possible to make the PR quite a bit simpler and at the same time, make the amount of time that the container filesystem is frozen as short as possible.

Instead of exposing any freeze/thaw APIs, we could have something like this on the runtime API:

```swift
  // RuntimeRoutes
  static let snapshotDisk = "com.apple.container.runtime/snapshotDisk"

  // RuntimeKeys (reuses existing destinationPath key; adds imagePath)
  static let imagePath = "imagePath"

  // RuntimeClient
  public func snapshotDisk(imagePath: String, destinationPath: String) async throws
```

where `snapshotDisk` in RuntimeService does freeze/clonefile/thaw in a single call.

@chavezMac I had a thought on this to future-proof the API.

What do you think about changing it to:

```swift
public func bootstrap(id: String, stdio: [FileHandle?], dynamicEnv: [String:String] = [:]) async throws {...}
```

We'd not expose this up to the CLI (`container start`) as generally, the env variables are baked in at create time. With this API we can address any other cases like SSH_AUTH_SOCK without breaking changes.

Do you think it'd work cleanly with what you have?

I do like the idea of a dynamicEnv API as a future-proof idea to support other bootstrap‑time env overrides without breaking changes. If we see more use cases beyond SSH, I’d be happy to prototype that in a separate PR.
The problem with not doing it now is that it guarantees there will be a breaking change.
I apologize for the delay in this request, I have been busy with other work. I plan on getting an updated PR for this by end of day, Friday!
It'd be better to get `source` and `destination` as `URL` type and convert them to string here.

The server uses `appRoot.formatted()` (which produces a human readable string) to encode the URL, but the client uses `URL(string:)` (which expects a proper URL format) to decode it. Would these always be compatible?
